chain.label: Mountain wave activity producing strong, localized, intermittent surface gusts at DEN
chain.trigger: significant mountain wave activity existed in the area at the time... resulted in strong, very localized, intermittent gusts at the airport's surface

chain.label: Night takeoff, limiting visual cues to wind conditions
chain.trigger: about 1818 mountain standard time... because of the darkness and the location of the wreckage

chain.label: ATC system did not require dissemination of the most adverse available wind (airport wind 35 kt gusting 40 kt)
chain.trigger: an air traffic control system that did not require or facilitate the dissemination of key, available wind information to the air traffic controllers and pilots

caused_by.evidence: widely variable surface winds across DEN airport locations... the AW displayed on the DEN ATCT RBDT was recorded by LLWAS sensor #2

chain.label: Local controller issued only runway 34R departure-end wind (270 at 27 kt), omitting the 35 kt/40 kt gust airport wind on his display
chain.trigger: he did not (nor was he clearly required to) provide information about the most adverse crosswind conditions that were displayed on his RBDT

caused_by.evidence: because DEN's system dictated only that the local controller provide departing pilots with departure wind information from preassigned sensors

chain.label: Crew unaware of the actual crosswind magnitude and gusts along the takeoff roll
chain.trigger: therefore, the pilots were not aware of the high winds that they would encounter during the takeoff roll

caused_by.evidence: the reported winds did not exceed Continental's maximum crosswind guidance of 33 knots

chain.label: Crew accepted takeoff clearance on runway 34R in strong crosswind
chain.trigger: given the wind-related information the pilots had, their decision to proceed with a takeoff on runway 34R as planned was reasonable

caused_by.evidence: if the accident pilots had received the most adverse available wind information... the captain would likely have decided to delay the departure or request a different runway

chain.label: Inadequate gusty-crosswind training: simulator applied no gusting winds below 50 ft agl
chain.trigger: its FFS atmospheric model software allowed for only steady state wind inputs—no gusting winds—below 50 feet agl

chain.label: Crosswind gust to about 45 knots struck the airplane at about 90 knots during the takeoff roll
chain.trigger: the left crosswind component increased from 30 knots to about 40 knots... a peak wind of about 45 knots at 1818:12

caused_by.evidence: a particularly strong wind gust (wind speeds as high as 45 knots) moved across the center of the airport, directly crossing the airplane's path
the accident flight was cleared for takeoff at 1817:26, and the takeoff initially progressed normally

chain.label: Airplane weathervaned rapidly left of the baseline heading despite 72 percent right rudder
chain.trigger: This strong crosswind gust increased the airplane's sideslip angle, significantly reduced the effect of the captain's 72-percent rudder pedal input, and weathervaned the airplane's nose further to the left

caused_by.evidence: the crosswind component increased above 40 knots for about 1.5 seconds

chain.label: Captain ceased right rudder input about 4 seconds before the excursion
chain.trigger: the captain's cessation of rudder input, which was needed to maintain directional control of the airplane, about 4 seconds before the excursion

caused_by.evidence: which led the captain to believe that the airplane was not responding to his rudder input... he abruptly relaxed the right pedal to its neutral position
because Continental's simulator training did not replicate the ground-level disturbances and gusting crosswinds... the captain was not adequately prepared to respond

chain.label: Captain used nosewheel steering tiller and full right control wheel at high speed, contrary to procedures
chain.trigger: The captain's use of the nosewheel steering tiller was contrary to company procedures and neither of these late control inputs was an effective method for turning the airplane at high speed

caused_by.evidence: the captain's use of tiller and full right control wheel in the 3 seconds before the excursion likely resulted from acute stress stemming from a sudden, unexpected threat, perceived lack of control, and extreme time pressure

chain.label: Loss of directional control; airplane veered left off the runway centerline
chain.trigger: the airplane continued to veer to the left... the airplane departed the runway at 1818:17 at a speed of about 110 knots

caused_by.evidence: instead of making another significant right rudder pedal input (the only control input that could have corrected the airplane's leftward veer off the runway), the captain began to make disorganized and ineffective control inputs
neither input had a significant effect on the airplane's heading

chain.label: Rejected takeoff initiated 2 to 4 seconds later than average response time
chain.trigger: the captain's initiation of a rejected takeoff was delayed by about 2 to 4 seconds because he was occupied with the nosewheel steering tiller and right control wheel input

caused_by.evidence: the captain did not have his right hand on the thrust levers during the excursion
at 1818:21, the captain called to reject the attempted takeoff

chain.label: Airplane departed left side of runway 34R at about 110 knots and crossed taxiway WC and a service road
chain.trigger: departed the left side of runway 34R during takeoff... crossed taxiway WC and an airport service road before coming to a stop

caused_by.evidence: the airplane continued to veer to the left
the pilots did not begin to reduce engine power until about 3 seconds after the airplane left the runway

chain.label: Airplane became airborne over uneven terrain and struck the ground; landing gear collapsed, fuselage broke, 3 G vertical spike
chain.trigger: as the airplane crossed the uneven terrain before coming to a stop, it became airborne, resulting in a jarring impact when it regained contact with the ground

caused_by.evidence: ground scars are visible from the edge of runway 34R, across taxiway WC and the airport service road, and up to the wreckage

chain.label: Captain and 5 passengers seriously injured; 41 minor injuries; substantial damage and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The captain and 5 of the 110 passengers were seriously injured... The airplane was substantially damaged

caused_by.evidence: the pilots' seats experienced both upward and downward crash forces in excess of their structural capabilities... the captain sustained multiple lumbar and thoracic spinal fractures
